hints.title: Locate the original vertex
hints.body: Complete the square in the original quadratic to find its minimum input and height.
hints.recap: The completed square identifies the input at which the quadratic reaches its minimum.
hints.pitfall: Both transformations act on the input; track their effect on the minimum position.

recall.reminder: The completed square identifies the input at which the quadratic reaches its minimum.

hints.title: Make the transformed inputs agree
hints.body: For each transformed function, set its inner expression equal to the original minimum input. Solve for its horizontal coordinate, then compare those coordinates.
hints.recap: A transformed point is found by making the new inner expression equal the old input.
hints.pitfall: An input multiplier changes horizontal coordinates by its reciprocal.
hints.pause: Derive the two minimum coordinates and equate them to express the scale parameter in terms of the shift.

recall.reminder: A transformed point is found by making the new inner expression equal the old input.

solution:
Since f(x)=(x−3)2−9, its minimum occurs at input 3 with height −9. The graph f(kx) reaches this height when kx=3, giving minimum (3k, −9). The graph f(x−c) reaches it when x−c=3, giving minimum (3+c, −9).

The points are identical precisely when 3k=3+c. Rearranging yields k=33+c, option B. For c>0 this is positive and below 1, consistent with the required horizontal stretch to move the minimum right.
knowledgePattern: Match the vertex under horizontal scaling and translation
